basis: Cryptophthalmos, syndactyly and airway malformations are defining; renal malformations occur in ~40%. Hearing and cleft anomalies omitted under the cap.
Varicella-zoster infection defined by vesicular skin lesions; damaging pulmonary and neurologic complications are uncommon.
Luteinizing hormone deficiency causes gonadal hormone insufficiency; sparse body hair reflects androgen deficiency rather than skin damage.
Diffuse carcinoma originates in the stomach; no other organ involvement is established as common.
Isolated spermatogenic failure and sperm structural abnormalities affect reproductive function without demonstrated endocrine dysfunction.
Gastrin-secreting neuroendocrine tumor and severe acid-mediated peptic disease define the syndrome; other endocrine tumors are minority associations.
Defined by ectopic hormone secretion; tumor origin and additional organ damage vary across this umbrella.
Iron metabolism disorder; hepatic fibrosis 80–99%, cardiomyopathy and arthropathy each 30–79%. Pigmentation alone does not establish skin damage.
HIV-associated enteric mucosal dysfunction causes chronic diarrhea after exclusion of other enteric infections.
Inherited cerebellar dysfunction or degeneration; additional organ disease is subtype-specific across this umbrella.
Species-defined fungal infection; pulmonary and ear infections occur, but the broad definition establishes neither site in most patients.
Thyrotropin-producing anterior pituitary neoplasm causes endocrine dysfunction; visual or cardiovascular damage is not established as common.
Demodex infestation causes inflammation of cutaneous hair follicles.
Chronic autoimmune inflammation of oral mucosa; cutaneous lichen planus is not intrinsic to every oral case.
Heterogeneous nuclear-lamina disorders with prominent muscle and skeletal phenotypes; cardiac, metabolic and neural damage vary substantially by subtype.
Inherited selective inability to perceive musk is an olfactory functional deficit; unspecified blindness lacks evidence of common involvement.
Inherited calcium dysregulation; direct renal calcium deposition is common in symptomatic infants and can cause persistent renal injury in ≥30% over the course.
Congenital secondary erythrocytosis is a blood-cell disorder; thrombosis is a potential complication rather than established common organ damage.
Developmental and cognitive impairment with neuronal migration abnormalities define the syndrome; renal and skeletal malformations are minority findings.
Defective steroidogenesis causes adrenal and gonadal hormone failure; pigmentation, vomiting and salt wasting do not establish other organ damage.
Congenital hand and foot deformities with joint contractures define the syndrome; high palate and hypotonia alone do not establish additional organ damage.
Chronic toxic injury directly affects multiple peripheral nerves.
Inherited trochlear nerve palsy is defined by superior oblique dysfunction and impaired ocular alignment or binocular vision.
Marrow failure and skin/nail dystrophy; oral leukoplakia 4/12 (~33%). Pulmonary fibrosis 3/12 (25%); separate pneumonitis count may overlap.
Intellectual disability and marfanoid skeletal habitus define the syndrome; strabismus lacks evidence of common involvement.
